source.quote: Primare's own page for the I25 Prisma, read 2026-11-25. Specification rows: « DAC » / « ESS ES9068A »; « Toslink » / « 4 x digital input »; « RCA » / « 2 x digital input »; « RCA » / « 1 x digital output »; « USB-B » / « 1 x digital input »; « USB-A » / « 1 x digital input ». Section text: « The DM36 is a full-featured digital to analog converter stage enabling up to PCM 384kHz/32bit and DSD 256 conversion, with upsampling options and MQA processing. » The page states NO per-input sample rate, NO bit depth per input, and NO native-versus-DoP distinction, and names no filter. The per-input figures recorded here come from Primare's own DM36 module page (https://primare.net/products/dm36/): « Inputs include 4 Toslink optical and 2 RCA coaxial for resolution of up to 192kHz/24 bit, and 1 USB B input for computer connection with resolution of up to 384kHz/32 bit and DSD256 (11.2MHz). » and « A new feature found in the DM36 is the PCM up-sampling option, which when the setting is enabled allows 16/44.1 and 24/48 kHz signals to be up-sampled to 24/88.2 kHz and 24/96 kHz respectively ».

facts.chip: « ESS ES9068A », inside a converter stage Primare calls the DM36 and fits across its range.

device_settings.why: « the PCM up-sampling option, which when the setting is enabled allows 16/44.1 and 24/48 kHz signals to be up-sampled to 24/88.2 kHz and 24/96 kHz respectively ». A setting, off by implication since the maker calls enabling it a choice. Left off for the reason applied to every optional resampler here - LUMIN's, FiiO's, Pro-Ject's, Aurender's: Auto has already chosen the rate and designed the filter.

_verification_des_conditions_faite: primare.net's « Cookies, Privacy & Terms » page was READ (Terms of Service section, last updated September 2017). Its only intellectual-property language is « The Site and all of its original content are the sole property of Primare », an ownership statement with a copyright notice - not a prohibition on use, reproduction or extraction. No Impressum or separate legal notice exists; the footer gives the company address.
_les_debits_par_entree_viennent_de_la_pa: This product page states the device figure - « The DM36 is a full-featured digital to analog converter stage enabling up to PCM 384kHz/32bit and DSD 256 conversion » - and gives no per-input rate. The per-input breakdown is on Primare's own page for the DM36 module: « Inputs include 4 Toslink optical and 2 RCA coaxial for resolution of up to 192kHz/24 bit, and 1 USB B input for computer connection with resolution of up to 384kHz/32 bit and DSD256 (11.2MHz). » Carrying it across rests on a correspondence that can be CHECKED rather than assumed: this page names the DM36 as its converter stage, and its own socket list - 4 Toslink, 2 RCA, 1 USB-B - matches the module page's count exactly, socket for socket. That is not analogy between siblings, which this catalogue refuses; it is one maker describing one named module in two places. The reasoning is written out so it can be contested, and if it is wrong it is wrong on all three Primare records at once.
